rq-wx-01.front: Which weather has the strongest evidence for moving Interior mule deer in fall?
rq-wx-01.back: Snow and cold. They trigger the move to winter range (85%).

rq-wx-03.front: Wind before and after a cold front?
rq-wx-03.back: Before: south or southwest. After: west or northwest, colder, pressure rising (70%).

rq-wx-04.front: Penn State, 30 winter storms: deer before the storm?
rq-wx-04.back: No real change in movement before storms (80%).

rq-wx-05.front: Penn State, 30 winter storms: deer during the storm?
rq-wx-05.back: They moved less during the storm (80%).

rq-wx-06.front: Glass the calm after a storm: fact or tip?
rq-wx-06.back: A tip. No study here measured movement right after a front.

rq-wx-07.front: Barometric pressure evidence for deer movement?
rq-wx-07.back: Weak and mixed. Do not cancel a hunt for it (Tip).

rq-wx-09.front: Time of day versus weather: which matters more for deer activity?
rq-wx-09.back: Time of day. Weather effects were smaller than the daily rhythm (65%).

rq-wx-11.front: Wyoming mule deer: what set migration timing?
rq-wx-11.back: Temperature and snowfall. Rifle season added only about 2% for does (85%).
